scope: Bounded implementation of fs/select.c and fs/aio.c time64 compat handlers, read-only review of parent-owned dispatch/time/futex/signal/net changes, and isolated compile-only validation of the disabled AIO translation unit. No full kernel build, SSH or hardware operations by this agent.
verdict: No blocking ABI/marshalling problem found in the reviewed source. 19 newly wired compat time64 calls have enabled subsystems; io_pgetevents_time64 has a correct source handler but remains ENOSYS with CONFIG_AIO=n. Runtime tests and final build verification belong to separate evidence.

assumptions: This is a CONFIG_ARM64=y, CONFIG_64BIT=y kernel, not a generic native 32-bit kernel backport.
The native timespec/itimerspec representations have 64-bit seconds; the supplied clock_adjtime64 __kernel_timex layout is confirmed separately by the ABI agent against native struct timex.
The syscall scalar arguments and simple pointed-to data have compatible widths; do not extend this reasoning to compound pointer/size structures.

details.403_404_406: Use existing get_timespec64/put_timespec64 and native k_clock operations.
details.405: Native timex is suitable only because its full layout matches the fixed-width time64 timex; ordinary ARM32 struct timex is not suitable. No native struct timex redesign was made.
details.407: New time64 clock_nanosleep deliberately uses TT_NATIVE and the 16-byte put_timespec64 restart copyout. Legacy clock_nanosleep keeps TT_COMPAT and the old 8-byte copyout.
details.408_411: The timer and timerfd native paths use 64-bit itimerspec fields; timer IDs, descriptors and flags are fixed-width.
details.412: The native utimensat array advances by 16-byte native timespec and uses get_timespec64 for both timestamps, including UTIME_NOW/OMIT handling.
details.418_419: Message byte buffers have no pointer-bearing structure, msg_prio is unsigned int/u32, and the timeout uses the native64 helper. No mq_attr or sigevent is passed to these two calls.
details.420: sembuf is a fixed-width element and the timeout goes through get_timespec64.
details.422: The shared native futex entry now parses with get_timespec64, validates timespec64 and converts using timespec64_to_ktime. Old compat futex remains separate; changing only its table without this parser update would mishandle nanosecond padding.
details.423: The native scheduler interval uses put_timespec64; pid is fixed-width.

required_compat_marshalling.reason: AArch32 fd_set words are 32-bit; sixth argument is exactly {u32 sigset_pointer, u32 sigsetsize}, not a pair of native 64-bit values.
required_compat_marshalling.implementation: Reuses compat_core_sys_select and get_compat_sigset; only timeout parsing/copyback uses get_timespec64 and poll_select_copy_remaining. The embedded pointer is expanded with compat_ptr.
required_compat_marshalling.signal_semantics: Preserves existing 4.19 saved_sigmask/ERESTARTNOHAND sequence and STICKY_TIMEOUTS/read-only timeout behavior, with no task_struct or restart_block layout change.

required_compat_marshalling.reason: pollfd is width-stable, but the signal set must retain compat ordering and sigsetsize validation.
required_compat_marshalling.implementation: Uses do_sys_poll and get_compat_sigset; 16-byte timeout read/write through native64 helpers. Existing 4.19 delayed mask restore on interruption is retained.

required_compat_marshalling.reason: The usig descriptor contains a 32-bit pointer and 32-bit size, and min_nr/nr are signed 32-bit arguments. A native table entry loses signed extension and can read the wrong descriptor.
required_compat_marshalling.implementation: New private struct __compat_aio_sigset_time64 has compat_uptr_t and compat_size_t; zero initialized, copied as 8 bytes and pointer passed through compat_ptr. get_compat_sigset plus local saved-mask handling mirror existing 4.19 semantics. Legacy buggy descriptor/handler is unchanged because this task preserves existing ABI and no old io_pgetevents entry is exposed in this arm64 table.
required_compat_marshalling.limitation: CONFIG_AIO remains disabled; the conditional syscall stub correctly returns ENOSYS. The implementation is not claimed runtime-tested under enabled AIO.

required_compat_marshalling.reason: mmsghdr, iovec and ancillary cmsghdr retain AArch32 layout even though timeout becomes time64.
required_compat_marshalling.implementation: Parent wrapper reads get_timespec64, converts to native kernel struct timespec without narrowing on arm64, and sets MSG_CMSG_COMPAT before calling the existing __sys_recvmmsg. Remaining timeout is copied as 16 bytes only when ret>0, matching existing semantics.
required_compat_marshalling.limitation: This does not add SO_TIMESTAMP_NEW/NS_NEW/ING_NEW; old compat ancillary timestamp fields remain time32.

required_compat_marshalling.reason: siginfo output layout and signal-set word representation remain AArch32.
required_compat_marshalling.implementation: Parent wrapper uses get_compat_sigset and copy_siginfo_to_user32 with a time64 timeout. timespec64_to_timespec is lossless on this 64-bit kernel, and the existing do_sigtimedwait validates timeout.

global_helpers.get_timespec64: The parent removes the ineffective CONFIG_64BIT_TIME guard for in_compat_syscall, so the upper 32 bits of tv_nsec padding are ignored for the new AArch32 ABI. Low 32-bit invalid nsec values still fail range checks at syscall use sites.
unchanged_legacy_contracts: COMPAT_USE_64BIT_TIME remains zero; compat_get_timespec64 and compat_put_timespec64 keep old 32-bit seconds.
The old syscall numbers and handlers are unchanged.
Native syscall numbers do not change; compat limit grows to 424, leaving 399-402 and 415 unimplemented.

correctness_fixes_beyond_v5_1.title: aio: Fix io_pgetevents() struct __compat_aio_sigset layout
correctness_fixes_beyond_v5_1.application: New time64 descriptor uses compat_uptr_t+compat_size_t and compat_ptr, rather than copying the old native-pointer definition.

correctness_fixes_beyond_v5_1.title: syscalls: fix compat_sys_io_pgetevents_time64 usage
correctness_fixes_beyond_v5_1.application: Number 416 maps to compat_sys_io_pgetevents_time64. Initial v5.1 and v5.15 release tables incorrectly used sys_io_pgetevents; this later upstream correction is intentionally included.

test_handoff: Guard-page tests for a 4-byte ARM32 fd_set and 8-byte pselect sig descriptor.
High signal-set bit and process-local interruption tests with original signal mask restored.
16-byte remaining timeout copyback and legacy 8-byte time32 behavior.
AIO=n must return ENOSYS; do not label the optional disabled subsystem operational.
Future enabled-AIO validation must include 8-byte usig guard, negative min_nr/nr sign extension and interrupted mask restoration.
not_done: No full kernel build or live test performed by this subagent; the AIO translation unit was compiled separately without linking.
No source edits after parent started compilation.
No conversion of old socket timestamp options, filesystem formats, libc ABI or unrelated 64-bit layouts.
